# Pesher Habakkuk Column 13 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Pesher Habakkuk Column 13 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 13:2 — "mixing in his fury" vs. "pouring out his fury" vs. "pouring out his rage"
| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "mixing-in his-fury" | Hebrew mesappech chemato — literally "pouring/mixing" |
| LOGOS | "pouring out his fury" | Formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "pouring out his rage" | "rage" for chemah |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "pouring out his fury." More natural English than "mixing in"; "fury" better than "rage" for chemah.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 13:14-15 — "did not circumcise the foreskin of his heart" vs. "refused to let God change his heart"
| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he-did-not circumcise the-foreskin-of his-heart" | Literal Hebrew metaphor |
| LOGOS | "he did not circumcise the foreskin of his heart" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "he refused to let God change his heart" | Dynamic interpretation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS literal rendering. The metaphor of heart-circumcision is a key biblical/Qumran image (cf. Deut 10:16) and must be preserved, not interpreted away.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 13:16 — "ways of excess" vs. "ways of drunkenness" vs. "a path of excess"
| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in-ways-of-excess" | Hebrew derakhei ha-revayah |
| LOGOS | "in ways of drunkenness" | Specifies the excess as drink |
| PNEUMA | "a path of excess" | Singular; generalized |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "in ways of excess" (EMET). The Hebrew revayah means "saturation/excess" — not exclusively drunkenness, though drink is in context. The broader term captures the pesher's moral critique.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---
*Total disagreements in Column 13: 3 | Covers Hab 2:15-17, 18-20*
